sections.title: The Perpetual Miracle Concept and Historical Context
sections.summary: Khalifa presents the thesis that Muhammad's miracle must be eternal and perpetual, unlike previous prophets' time-limited miracles. He argues the Quran itself is this perpetual miracle, witnessed across 1400 years as scientific discoveries confirm Quranic statements. The author distinguishes Muhammad's miracle from Moses and Jesus by claiming it is accessible to all generations, not limited to eyewitnesses in a specific place and time.

sections.title: The Number 19 and Bismillah Verse Analysis
sections.summary: Khalifa presents the discovery that the first Quranic verse ('In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful') consists of exactly 19 letters. He claims each word in this opening verse appears in the entire Quran in multiples of 19: 'Name' 19 times, 'Allah' 2,698 times (19×142), 'Al-Rahman' 57 times (19×3), and 'Al-Rahim' 114 times (19×6). He cites historical word-frequency references to verify these counts and argues this cannot be coincidence but proves divine authorship.

sections.title: Qur'anic Initials and Their Mysterious Significance

The author links this to revelation history, noting that Sura 96 (first revelation) is number 19 from the end of the Quran and contains 19 verses.
